task:
FIX AN INSPECT BUG: THE SELECTED BODY CARRIES OVER INTO A DIFFERENT SYSTEM. CHANGE apps/web/src/lib/components/SystemDetail.svelte AND ITS TESTS ONLY (plus SystemOverlay.svelte or routes/inspect/+page.svelte only if a test proves they need a change). NO API, MODEL, STORAGE OR DEPENDENCY CHANGES.

The defect (reproduced on main 4d54e2e4 by the 2026-10-31 audit, finding A2):
- `SystemDetail.svelte` keeps `let selectedBodyId = $state<number | undefined>()` (line 39), and `selectedBody` (line 93) looks that number up in whatever system is loaded now.
- Body ids are Frontier BodyIDs, which only mean something within one system. Inspect and the Explore overlay (`SystemOverlay.svelte`) reuse the same `SystemDetail` instance when `id64` changes.
- So: select body 3 in system A, go to system B, which also has a body 3. B immediately shows "Selected body" for its own body 3, although nothing was selected there. The 3D system scene (`systemScene`, line 84) gets the same stale id.

The fix:
1. Scope the selection to its system. For example, store `{ systemId: id64, bodyId }`, and derive the selected body only when `selection.systemId` equals the current `id64`. Clearing on change is also acceptable, as long as no stale id can ever reach `selectedBody` or `systemScene`, even for one render.
2. Changing `id64` shows no selection, both when the new system is already cached and while it is still loading. The old selection must not reappear when the load finishes.
3. A refetch or reload of the SAME system keeps the selection (for example, the Reload action and a background refetch).
4. Navigating A → B → back to A shows no selection in A (a fresh visit; nothing to restore).
5. Accessibility (audit F13): the selected-body card currently has `aria-live="polite"` on the whole `<article>`, so screen readers read out the entire changing card. Remove `aria-live` from the article. Add one visually hidden polite live region that announces only "Selected <body name>" when the user selects a body, and announces nothing when the selection clears because the system changed. Keep the article's `data-selected-body-id` attribute.

TESTS (the existing SystemDetail test file and its conventions; `SystemDetailTestHost.svelte` is the host the audit used):
- The audit's reproduction, kept as a permanent test:
  - mock `getSystem`, and seed the query cache for a second system (id64 42, named "Second System") whose bodies include id 3;
  - render the first system and click body 3 (the article shows `data-selected-body-id="3"`);
  - rerender with id64 42 and wait for the "Second System" heading;
  - expect no `article`.
  Use the fixtures `referenceSystemDetail`/`referenceSystemRatings` from `$lib/api/v3-system-fixtures`, as the audit did.
- The same with the second system NOT cached: `getSystem` resolves it later (deferred promise). No article while loading, and none after it resolves.
- Same-system refetch: after selecting body 3, invalidate or refetch the same system's query; the selection is still shown.
- A → B → A: no selection on return.
- The 3D scene input receives no selected id after the system changes. Assert on whatever the component passes to the scene (`systemScene`), or through the existing scene test seam if there is one.
- The live region: selecting a body announces "Selected <name>"; the article has no `aria-live`; changing systems announces nothing.

VALIDATION: in apps/web: `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, `pnpm check`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm format:check`, `pnpm test` (report file and test counts), `pnpm build`. SUMMARY: the root cause, the changed lines, and each new test with its result.
